variable_coverage.construction: Three-day firm return adjusted by a market benchmark over days −1,0,+1. The paper does not give the market-return series or arithmetic formula. Sample inclusion also requires the documented nonoverlap screens around earnings announcements and dividend declarations.

Forecast revision surprise multiplied by SUP: current analyst EPS forecast minus the same analyst’s most recent same-firm forecast, divided by CRSP share price two days before revision; SUP uses the analyst’s prior two-year comparison with contemporaneous I/B/E/S consensus and actual EPS. Exact category equality at 80% overlaps the Normal definition.
Same forecast revision surprise multiplied by NOR; Table 4 labels Normal as 20% to 80%, overlapping Inferior at 20% and Superior at 80%.
Same forecast revision surprise multiplied by INF; Table 4 labels Inferior as 20% and below, overlapping Normal at 20%.

design_coverage.reason: No cluster or standard-error correction is specified.
The source calls the analysis a regression but does not name the underlying estimator.
The Table 4 equation reports only an intercept and the three revision-surprise/category interactions; no fixed effects are reported.
No regression weights are reported for the selected Table 4 fit.

implementation_issues.description: The article reports a regression but does not name the underlying estimator, standard-error method, or clustering procedure for Table 4.
The 80% category definitions overlap at exactly 20% and 80%; the article does not state which category receives boundary observations.

The dependent variable is called three-day market-adjusted return, but no market index or arithmetic adjustment rule is reported. CRSP daily return/market index candidates remain unverified for this definition.

The article requires I/B/E/S, Compustat and CRSP intersection data and same-firm analyst histories, but does not specify exact identifier-link vintage/selection rules for recycled tickers and analyst-firm identity.

review_notes: Retained Table 4’s 80% threshold column; other thresholds are sensitivity checks. The sample requires all source-stated analyst history screens: at least five brokerages in each year 1988–1994, at least five same-firm forecasts in the prior two years with at least one in each year, no fiscal-year-end change over the seven years, and nonoverlap with revision/earnings/dividend windows. Do not collapse prior forecast history with later reporting dates of its realized EPS. The 20%/80% cutpoints overlap exactly as printed.
